function_analysis: Unchanged for this map. After four rounds all evaluated concepts give 0.3-1.5 % objective gain against silicone foul-release; the clean-surface friction (wall_shear) has not been probed, and durability of soft layers (tearing, oil/sol leaching) remains the common weak point.

requirements.name: friction_drag_reduction
requirements.criterion: Lowers the time-averaged hull friction resistance over the service interval compared with the conventional biocide-free foul-release coating.

requirements.name: no_toxic_biocides
requirements.criterion: Releases no biocides, heavy metals, or other toxic or persistent substances (including leaching oils or polymer fragments) into seawater.

requirements.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirements.criterion: Keeps adhesion, integrity and function for at least 5 years in seawater, including abrasion, UV at the waterline, cathodic protection and hydrolysis.

requirements.name: fouling_control
requirements.criterion: Limits slime and macrofouling (or allows its easy release at service speeds or by gentle cleaning) throughout the interval, including idle periods.

requirements.name: bionic_mechanism
requirements.criterion: The working mechanism is genuinely derived from a biological model.

requirements.name: practical_application
requirements.criterion: Can be applied to large steel hulls with shipyard processes at a cost comparable to premium coatings and without continuous energy or material supply.

objective_statement: Time-averaged hull frictional resistance of a merchant ship over a 5-year docking interval in seawater (mixed operating profile around 12-16 kn with idle periods), including the drag added by slime and macrofouling and by coating degradation, not the friction of a freshly applied clean surface.
baseline_statement: Conventional biocide-free silicone (PDMS/fluoropolymer-modified) foul-release coating averaged over the same 5-year interval, i.e. in its typical in-service state after 12-24 months with a light-to-medium slime layer and occasional macrofouling during idle periods.
mechanism_classes_considered: graded_stiffness (anisotropic compliant wall interacting with near-wall turbulence)
graded_stiffness (oil-free supersoft network with fibre reinforcement, low extractables)
graded_stiffness (tiled stiff skin on a soft bed)
analogues_considered: Palm and grass stems and kelp stipes with inclined fibres (anisotropic compliance), cf. Grosskreutz's anisotropic compliant walls
Sea-ice pack: floes decoupled by leads on the ocean surface
DNS of anisotropic compliant walls (Fukagata et al.) showing drag changes at low Reynolds number

candidates.title: Inclined-fibre anisotropic compliant skin: palm-stem fibre angle tuned to the viscous sublayer
candidates.summary: A 300 um soft silicone layer with embedded microfibres inclined at about 45 degrees against the flow, like the inclined fibre helices in palm and grass stems, makes the wall move mainly streamwise when a pressure or shear fluctuation acts on it. Tuned so that its natural frequency matches near-wall turbulence at 12-16 kn, such anisotropic compliant walls produce a small effective streamwise slip that lowers skin friction slightly; the same layer is soft enough for easier fouling release.

back_of_envelope.quantity: time-averaged hull friction reduction vs conventional foul-release coating over 5 years
back_of_envelope.formula: natural frequency of the layer (1/t)*sqrt(G/rho) = (1/3e-4)*sqrt(1e5/1000) = 3.3e4 rad/s vs near-wall turbulence u_tau^2/nu = 0.16^2/1e-6 = 2.6e4 rad/s (matched); wall streamwise velocity ~0.3 u_tau acts as effective slip b+ ~ 0.3; Delta U+ ~ b+ gives dCf/Cf ~ 2*Delta U+/U+ = 2*0.3/28 = 2 % on the clean surface, discounted for fouling covering the wall and ageing: ~1 %

candidates.main_risk: Anisotropic compliant-wall drag reduction has only been shown at low Reynolds numbers in DNS and a few tests; at ship Reynolds numbers the wall may instead flutter or amplify disturbances and raise drag, and slime covers the compliant response.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: Kramer's dolphin-inspired compliant coatings and Grosskreutz's anisotropic compliant walls. New: realising the anisotropy with inclined embedded microfibres (plant stem fibre angle) inside a foul-release silicone, and tuning it to ship-speed sublayer frequencies.
candidates.baseline: Conventional biocide-free silicone foul-release coating averaged over the same 5-year interval in service.
candidates.inspiration_source: Palm and grass stems and kelp stipes: cellulose fibres wound at an angle (microfibril and fibre angle) give direction-dependent compliance, so the organ shears and bends preferentially along one direction.
candidates.physical_mechanism: A wall that responds to near-wall pressure and shear fluctuations mainly with streamwise motion, in phase with the near-wall velocity, acts on average like a small streamwise slip at the wall; the effective slip length b shifts the log law up by Delta U+ ~ b+, lowering skin friction by about 2*Delta U+/U+. Inclined fibres couple wall-normal loading into streamwise displacement; the layer thickness and modulus tune its natural frequency to the near-wall frequency u_tau^2/nu.

parameters.name: effective_slip_length
parameters.justification: b+ = 0.3 with nu/u_tau = 6.3 um; from wall streamwise velocity ~0.3 u_tau in anisotropic compliant-wall DNS.

parameters.name: equivalent_laminar_gap
parameters.justification: Gap h with h+ = U+ = 28 (h = 28*nu/u_tau) that reproduces the turbulent skin friction in a Couette model.

parameters.name: layer_thickness
parameters.justification: Sets the natural frequency with the shear modulus.

parameters.name: layer_shear_modulus
parameters.justification: Soft silicone with fibres; matches near-wall frequency at this thickness.

parameters.name: fibre_angle
parameters.justification: About 45 degrees against the flow, as in Grosskreutz's walls and plant fibre helices (rad).

parameters.name: wall_velocity
parameters.justification: Ship speed ~10 kn equivalent for the Couette upper wall (m/s).

candidates.title: Oil-free supersoft palm-stem layer: bottle-brush silicone matrix with embedded fibres and near-zero extractables
candidates.summary: The palm-stem anisotropic release layer needs an ultra-soft matrix, and ultra-soft silicones are normally oil-extended or have large sol fractions that leach and stiffen the layer over years. Here the matrix is a solvent-free bottle-brush PDMS elastomer (side chains dilute entanglements, E ~0.1 MPa with sol fraction ~2 %), reinforced by normal-aligned fibres as in palm stems, so the layer keeps its softness and releases almost no mobile silicone over 5 years.

back_of_envelope.quantity: time-averaged hull friction reduction vs conventional foul-release coating over 5 years
back_of_envelope.formula: leaching flux J = D*c_sol/L: design 1e-15*20/3e-4 = 6.7e-11 vs oil-containing conventional 1e-15*45/1.5e-4 = 3e-10 kg/m^2/s (-78 %); a soft layer that does not stiffen keeps the ~50 % lower release stress for the whole interval instead of losing part of it after 1-2 years: +0.3-0.5 % on top of the release benefit, ~1.3 % total

candidates.main_risk: Bottle-brush elastomers have low tear strength and are costly to make at coating scale; without oil the initial release performance may be lower than oil-containing commercial coatings.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: the palm-stem layer in this map, oil-containing foul-release coatings and supersoft bottle-brush elastomers from the lab. New: using a solvent-free bottle-brush network as the soft matrix of a fibre-reinforced foul-release layer to remove oil and sol leaching, the degradation path of soft coatings.
candidates.baseline: Conventional biocide-free silicone foul-release coating (with 3-5 wt% free silicone oil, as in many commercial systems) averaged over the same 5-year interval in service.
candidates.inspiration_source: Monocot stems (palms, bamboo): stiff vascular fibre bundles in a soft parenchyma that keeps its properties without any mobile component (turgor and bound water only).
candidates.domain: Polymer transport / degradation of soft coatings
candidates.physical_mechanism: The mobile species in a silicone coating (free oil or unreacted sol chains) diffuse to the surface and leach; their loss stiffens the layer and, for oil, removes the slippery surface film. The leaching flux is J = D*c_mobile/L. A bottle-brush network reaches very low modulus with few mobile chains, and the fibres give the compressive stiffness, so the mobile concentration is low and the degradation rate of the layer's softness falls.

parameters.name: mobile_concentration
parameters.justification: Sol fraction ~2 wt% of a bottle-brush elastomer (kg/m^3).

parameters.name: mobile_diffusivity
parameters.justification: Diffusion of silicone oligomers in a crosslinked network.

parameters.name: fibre_volume_fraction
parameters.justification: Normal-aligned fibres as in the parent.

candidates.title: Pack-ice tiled skin on a soft bed: stiff skin cut into floes to stop load spreading and contain damage
candidates.summary: The glacier soft-bed coating lost part of its benefit because a continuous stiff skin spreads a barnacle's load over about 1.6 mm around its base. Here the 50 um skin is laser- or mask-segmented into 0.5 mm tiles separated by 20 um gaps filled with the soft bed material, like sea-ice floes separated by leads: each tile moves on its own, so the bed's compliance is kept, cuts and tears stop at tile edges, and hull strain is taken up by the gaps.

back_of_envelope.quantity: time-averaged hull friction reduction vs conventional foul-release coating over 5 years
back_of_envelope.formula: effective compliance C = 3*t_bed/E_bed*(a/(a+l))^2 + 3*t_skin/E_skin with spreading length l limited to half a tile (0.25 mm) instead of the shear-lag length 1.6 mm: (5/5.25)^2 = 0.91 vs 0.57; sigma_c ratio sqrt(4.5e-10/(1.05e-8*0.91)) = 0.22 (-78 %) vs 0.27 for the continuous skin; damage contained to single tiles: ~1.8 %

candidates.main_risk: The tile gaps are 20 um grooves of soft material that may be preferred settlement sites and that tear under fender contact, and segmenting a skin on a ship hull is an extra, slow process.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: the glacier soft-bed coating in this map and segmented thermal-barrier or scale-like armour coatings. New: segmentation of the stiff protective skin of a foul-release bilayer so that load spreading and crack propagation are limited to one tile.
candidates.baseline: Conventional biocide-free silicone foul-release coating (uniform topcoat, E about 1 MPa, 150 um) averaged over the same 5-year interval in service.
candidates.inspiration_source: Sea-ice pack on the ocean: stiff ice floes separated by leads of open water or soft slush move independently on the water, so stresses and fractures stay local instead of propagating through a continuous sheet.
candidates.domain: Fracture mechanics of layered soft coatings
candidates.physical_mechanism: A rigid fouler base bonded to the surface releases when G = tau^2*C/2 exceeds w; C is the areal compliance of the stack under the base. A continuous stiff skin spreads the load over a shear-lag length l = sqrt(E_s t_s t_b/G_b) beyond the base, enlarging the loaded bed area and lowering C by (a/(a+l))^2. Tiles smaller than the base limit l to half a tile, keeping C close to 3*t_bed/E_bed, while the gaps stop cracks and take up hull strain.

parameters.name: tile_size
parameters.justification: Smaller than the barnacle base (10 mm diameter).
